Liam to run a 512-token perf baseline with customer's example prompts and share results by 2025-11-14
Customer to share PII policy + sample prompt set by 2025-11-12
Schedule on-prem pilot run with SEs (week of 2025-11-17)

Liam Ortega - Run perf baseline on customer's 512-token prompts and share results - 2025-11-14

summary: Follow-up renewal check-in. Sunstone is leaning toward a 12-month extension with Dedicated capacity into EU and APAC for regulatory coverage. Key concerns: KMS/in-field key control, SOC2 evidence, latency for EU region, and pricing for burst capacity. SE will run a perf baseline with customer prompts to validate latency/cost assumptions; AE to send updated pricing; plan pilot for private/air-gapped on-prem path if SOC/KMS requirements require it.
topics: renewal options, dedicated capacity sizing, multi-region (EU/APAC) onboarding, private on-prem pilot, security and KMS, SOC2/audit docs, pricing tradeoffs (latency vs cost, burst vs reserved), timeline for procurement
transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-11-06 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~47m
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Liam (Redwood SE), Naomi (CSM), Priya (Sunstone Head of ML), Carlos (Platform Lead), Diane (Procurement), Jamal (Security)

Summary: quick renewal check-in, talked through Dedicated sizing for EU + APAC, sovereignty questions, and next steps for a pilot and updated quote. Some audio dropouts; transcript has occasional mis-attributions.

[00:00] Maya: ok thanks everyone for joining, um today is just a renewal and capacity check, wanted to see where you landed after the doc we sent last week.
[00:21] Priya: yeah thanks Maya, we reviewed it. we're, um, pretty aligned on moving forward but want a firmer view on latency from EU and cost for burst. also we've got the security team asking about key control.
[00:35] Carlos: and timeline, procurement wants to know if we can finish 12-month extension and have EU activated by mid-december. is that realistic?
[00:47] Maya: got it. quick answer is yes in Hosted for EU, but for Dedicated and private onprem, depends on capacity and provisioning windows. Liam, want to add on regional activation time?
[00:58] Liam: yeah sure. so for Dedicated EU pool if we already have quota it's typically 2-3 weeks to provision and verify; private/V P C or on-prem is longer, usually 4-8 weeks depending on you know rack access and K M S integrations, ping us with your KMS provider and we can detail.
[01:22] Jamal: when you say K M S integrations — do you support customer-managed keys with H S M? our compliance requires in-field key control and key rotation auditing.
[01:31] Liam: we do support KMS/H S M integrations. there are two patterns: customer-managed keys in their cloud K M S (recommended), or H S M-backed keys for on-prem. we'll share architecture diagrams; but there is a little ops work to wire up audit logs.
[01:47] Diane: procurement question — if we move to Dedicated and commit for 12 months, what's the pricing delta to include EU and APAC regions plus burst? we need number for budget planning.
[02:03] Maya: we'll produce a revised cost model — two options: reserved capacity across 3 regions vs single-region + cross-region failover. reserved is more predictable but costs more up-front; cross-region fallbacks reduce reserved units but add latency risk. I'll send the spreadsheet.
[02:24] Priya: latency is big for some of our inference touchpoints, like triage classification where 200-400ms matters. do you have numbers for token-level latency from EU region?
[02:36] Liam: baseline numbers in our catalog are there, but they're often optimistic; we'd rather run your prompt set. we can run a perf baseline with your sample prompts and the 512-token slices to measure p95 latency and cost per 1k tokens.
[02:51] Priya: great — we'll share a set but note many prompts include PHI; we need to ensure data handling during the test is compliant.
[03:01] Naomi: yes for the perf run we'll set it up in a redacted test VPC or use synthetic inputs. we can also redact with the prompt replacements you supply.
[03:12] Carlos: ok on the pilot, is it possible to do a short on-prem test in one of our edge DCs? we want to validate cold start and kv cache behavior under load.
[03:24] Liam: on-prem pilot is doable. depends on hardware — we have a recommended list. for K V cache behavior, we'll need to enable continuous batching and we'll instrument traces so you can see the KV hit rates.
[03:37] Jamal: regarding audit evidence — can you provide SOC two documentation, pen test summary, and encryption at rest/in transit proofs?
[03:45] Maya: yes we will share SOC2 attestation and pen test high-level summary. fullname docs are typically in our security portal; I'll send an invite.
[03:54] Diane: procurement also asks about contract amendment language for the 12-month extension and SLAs around latency — can we get sample contract terms?
[04:05] Maya: yep. we'll include optional SLA add-ons for p95 latency and plan-level uptime. Legal can draft amendment language post-quote.
[04:15] Priya: any concern about model variants? we currently run a mix of open weights and our tuned fork; do you support multi-model routing with fallbacks to smaller quantized variants when overloaded?
[04:29] Liam: absolutely. our routing supports model variants and automatic fallback — for example from full-float to q4 or q8 variants to maintain throughput. that helps with cost vs latency tradeoffs.
[04:41] Priya: ok good, we want to preserve quality.
[04:45] [crosstalk]
[04:53] Carlos: a question on burst capacity: how do you meter burst vs reserved? is billing per token during burst peak, and is there a different unit price?
[05:02] Maya: yes, burst uses pay-as-you-go pricing on top of committed units. the unit price during burst is typically higher — we can model different scenarios in the spreadsheet so you can see blended unit economics.
[05:15] Diane: procurement will need a projected cost for Q1 if we extend now, and also the cancellation terms for scaling down after three months.
[05:26] Maya: we'll put that scenario in. cancellation/amendment terms are usually in the contract appendix; we can propose a 30-60 day notice window for scale-downs.
[05:36] Priya: on data residency — for EU we need logs not leave EU for more than 24 hours, and all audit logs to be stored in EU K M S. is that supported?
[05:47] Liam: yes regional log retention is supported for Dedicated; for Hosted we'd need to do a Private control plane or EU-hosted tenant to guarantee that. on-prem obviously keeps everything local.
[06:00] Jamal: does Redwood provide per-token cost breakdown and tracing for prompts that leak PII so we can reconcile billing?
[06:10] Naomi: we have token-level cost and request tracing in the Console with optional retention. we can filter by session and export audit logs to your S3 or internal SIEM.
[06:21] Priya: perfect. that helps with our internal chargeback.
[06:27] Maya: ok to recap — you want a revised quote for a 12-month commitment covering US/EU/APAC Dedicated with burst uplift; SE to run perf baseline on your prompts; share SOC2 and K M S architecture docs; and plan an on-prem pilot if compliance needs push us there. anything else?
[06:45] Carlos: can you also add a single-region reserved + cross-region fallback option in the pricing so we can compare?
[06:52] Maya: yes will include that.
[06:55] Diane: timeline — procurement needs final numbers by Nov 18 to get approvals for December activation.
[07:03] Maya: we'll aim for Nov 10 quote and perf results the following week.
[07:09] Priya: quick tech question — are there any known perf regressions for sequence lengths over 1024 tokens? we've seen spikes at 1.2k.
[07:19] Liam: longer sequences amplify memory and kernel selection cost; we tune kernels for ranges, but yes p95 can spike for >1k sequences. the perf run will include 1k+ slices.
[07:36] Priya: ok thanks.
[07:40] [longer silence, 2 min audio glitch]
[09:55] Maya: while we wait I'll note competitors — MegaCloud AI pitched dedicated nodes but their KMS story was weaker; NimbusServe had lower headline cost but no EU private tenant.
[10:12] Priya: noted. we care more about audit and keys than small price deltas.
[10:20] Jamal: also can you summarize your incident response and breach notification timelines?
[10:28] Naomi: yes SRR: we have standard incident response with 72-hour notification for material security incidents; we can push for faster notification in the SLA.
[10:38] Diane: procurement needs SOC2 in the package and a pointer to the pen test.
[10:44] Maya: will do.
[10:48] Carlos: ok logistics — if we do on-prem pilot, which team at Sunstone needs to own rack prep and network peering?
[10:57] Priya: Platform will own that (Carlos), Procurement will handle contracts (Diane), Security (Jamal) for K M S and audit.
[11:05] Liam: great, once we have the prompt set and KMS provider info we'll size the pilot hardware and send a checklist.
[11:13] Maya: any blockers to proceeding with quote?
[11:16] Diane: none besides final budget approval, but we should be fine if the numbers match the model.
[11:22] Priya: timeline comfortable, assuming perf numbers look good.
[11:25] Maya: perfect. we'll target Nov 10 for the quote and set up the perf run; schedule for pilot week of Nov 17 if needed.
[11:34] [wrap up and quick recaps]
[11:40] Maya: I'll send meeting notes and a shared folder for SOC docs and the quote. Liam will ping for perf inputs. Naomi will schedule follow-up call for Nov 13 to review baseline.
[11:52] Priya: thanks everyone.
[11:55] Meeting end.

Notes on transcript: some timestamps approximate; occasional filler words removed for clarity. There are a few mis-heard acronyms like 'V P C' split and 'K M S' in pieces – verify with attachments.
